analysis:
This batch has two documentation-only changes: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/checkpoint-row-encoder.md, lines 1-8) and an added paragraph in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1602-1609). No executable code, config, keys, endpoints or crypto parameters are in the supplied evidence.

The prose says quantized checkpoint export now prepares buffers and its check once per segment instead of once per row, and still writes the scalar codec's exact bytes. It also says the donor stream retires only after the complete checkpoint is published (EngineLoopV2.finishAfterCompletePrefixPublication). This touches the encrypted prefix-cache surface in T-041/TB-007. The doc claims no change to at-rest format, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, scope salting or DBK3 AAD, so no threat-model assumption is invalidated by the docs themselves.

The only security-relevant risk is in the underlying implementation, NativeQuantizedCheckpointTensorSource.swift, which is not supplied. Hoisting a per-row check to once per segment could drop bounds or shape validation. The "identical bytes" claim is also unverified. Unsupplied code may need review for bounds, validation and byte-equivalence. The doc also notes that export time is added to the donor response's end. This is a latency note and is not newly exploitable beyond the already-accepted TTFT/timing oracle (SEC-035). The base-text excerpts of inference.md are unchanged context. No findings.
